description: Guide-specific executable candidate graph derived from the hash-bound Inner Signal r02 self-hypnosis guide; separate from the canonical production graph and existing inner-child/somatic bundle.

sourceAuthority.snapshotMethod: reader-visible text extraction from exact hash-bound HTML master; native-object markup excluded from graph source text

nodes.title: Orient and preserve stopping/return capacity first
recommendations: Pause inward work when present safety, orientation, stopping, or return capacity is not intact.
Use ordinary room/body/time orientation and available human support before deeper work.
avoid: Do not deepen trance, interpret memories, or make consequential commitments while disoriented or unable to stop.
successSignals: The person can identify the present setting, stop the exercise, and return to ordinary awareness.

requiredNuance: A difficult feeling can be wanted and workable while orientation and choice remain intact.
forbiddenOverclaims: Do not infer incapacity from a trauma label alone.

nodes.title: Choose the purpose and scope before entering
recommendations: Choose a manageable purpose: exploration, positive resource development, rehearsal, or simple practice.
Match depth to current capacity rather than treating every session as trauma work.
avoid: Do not make hidden-truth discovery the default goal.
successSignals: The session has a bounded purpose and a known stopping/return route.

nodes.title: Restore choice when outside or internal influence is steering
recommendations: Name the influence, separate observation from suggestion, and recover the ability to agree, disagree, or delay.
Use reality testing without assuming all influence is malicious.
avoid: Do not confuse soft, spiritual, therapeutic, or loving language with proof that choice is intact.
successSignals: The person can state their own position and compare it with the influence acting on them.

nodes.title: Gather attention without disappearing
recommendations: Use a fitting induction style and let actual responses guide pacing.
Keep the person able to modify, reject, or end suggestions.
avoid: Do not force a prescribed sensation, depth, metaphor, or relaxation response.
successSignals: Attention becomes more absorbed while stopping and return remain available.

nodes.title: Use a deliberate learned cue for easier future entry
recommendations: After full entry and return are familiar, pair a user-chosen word or gesture with the familiar receptive state.
Test the cue only in separately chosen practice and retire it if it intrudes or stops fitting.
avoid: Do not train or use a trance re-entry cue while driving, operating equipment, swimming, or responsible for someone needing attention.
Do not treat a cue as an irresistible command.
successSignals: Deliberate use may shorten entry without reducing the person’s ability to decline, redirect, or return.

requiredNuance: A trance-entry cue and an everyday alert-calming cue have different intended effects.
forbiddenOverclaims: Do not promise instant induction or perfect deconditioning.

nodes.title: Come all the way back and verify reorientation
recommendations: End the session deliberately, restore room/body/time orientation, voluntary movement, open eyes, and alertness.
Treat the return as a demonstrated state change, not as words that automatically prove completion.
avoid: Do not leave a vague or indefinite altered-state instruction active between sessions.
successSignals: The person is oriented, voluntarily moving, eyes open when appropriate, and alert enough for ordinary activity.

nodes.title: Hold the inner meeting without forcing a cast of characters
recommendations: Let the younger state, protector, whole self, heart, or another useful frame appear if it actually fits.
Keep Nurturer, Protector, and Leader/Guide functions available without requiring role-play.
avoid: Do not turn every sensation, urge, or silence into proof of a part.
successSignals: A useful relationship with the present experience emerges without losing present-day adult choice.

nodes.title: Let the next invitation grow from what actually happened
recommendations: Notice one thing accurately, make one fitting invitation, then leave enough silence to receive the response.
Let explicit mismatch, new information, or a changed bodily response alter the next move.
avoid: Do not keep following the script when the live response has changed the problem.
successSignals: The next prompt is traceable to the actual response rather than the script’s expected trajectory.

nodes.title: Treat bodily response as information, not an explanation of itself
recommendations: Track tightening, softening, movement impulses, numbness, warmth, distance, or other changes as observations.
Ask what changed and whether the invitation fits before assigning meaning.
avoid: Do not infer truth, falsity, a protector, a memory, or a cause from one bodily response alone.
successSignals: The observation remains distinct from the interpretation.

requiredNuance: Somatic authority can guide tolerance, readiness, preference, and response without settling external historical truth.

nodes.title: Change the amount of contact instead of forcing through
recommendations: Move closer to, farther from, or between difficult and neutral/resource experience according to the actual response.
Use smaller contact when intensity rises faster than reflective capacity.
avoid: Do not equate more intensity with more therapeutic depth.
successSignals: The person can stay in workable contact without losing the ability to observe, choose, and return.

nodes.title: Offer the care or distance that is actually wanted
recommendations: Let the Nurturer offer warmth, the Protector enact a boundary, and the Leader help with later action when those functions fit.
If a younger state says “don’t come closer,” respect the distance and notice what follows.
avoid: Do not treat a correct-sounding nurturing speech as proof that the care was received.
successSignals: The response shows whether the offered care, boundary, or distance is useful now.

nodes.title: Use hypnosis for love, play, confidence, creativity, or rehearsal too
recommendations: A session may deliberately develop warmth, play, confidence, spiritual communion, creativity, or rehearsal of a chosen action.
Judge a resource by what it actually does for this person rather than by how positive it sounds.
avoid: Do not require a wound, hidden cause, or child-state to justify practice.
successSignals: The selected resource increases useful capacity or supports a chosen real-world action.

nodes.title: Use a short regular practice to build fluency
recommendations: Use the short practice to rehearse entry, responsive listening, return, and one grounded follow-through.
avoid: Do not turn daily practice into compulsory deep processing.
successSignals: Self-hypnosis becomes easier to conduct without a script or app.

nodes.title: Use deeper practice only when current capacity supports it
recommendations: Use longer practice when orientation, stopping, return, and enough adult capacity are available.
Return to a smaller dose when deeper work destabilizes daily functioning.
avoid: Do not treat the weekly format as permission to intensify automatically.
successSignals: Depth increases while ordinary-life functioning and return capacity remain intact.

nodes.title: Capacity before content
recommendations: Prioritize the ability to stay present, stop, return, and function over obtaining more content.
When current capacity narrows, reduce dose or move to support rather than treating the resistance as something to break.
avoid: Do not make trauma disclosure, memory retrieval, or intensity a test of courage.
successSignals: The work stays inside a range the person can actually metabolize and leave.

nodes.title: When you dissociate or feel unreal, restore contact before interpretation
recommendations: Widen attention to the room and ordinary sensory contact; shorten or end the inner exercise as needed.
Use fractionation/return practice to strengthen voluntary movement into and out of internal focus.
avoid: Do not treat loss of orientation as therapeutic depth.
successSignals: Present-time orientation returns and the person can choose whether to continue.

nodes.title: Let analysis and intuition correct each other
recommendations: During the experience, keep enough judgment to reject implausible or unwelcome suggestions; do extended verification afterward.
If analysis is interrupting every moment, defer nonurgent fact-checking until after full return.
avoid: Do not ask the person to switch off critical judgment.
successSignals: The person can remain absorbed without surrendering the ability to question or later verify.

nodes.title: Check grandiosity, bliss, and spiritual bypass against ordinary reality
recommendations: Compare expansive conclusions with ordinary functioning, relationships, evidence, sleep, and the ability to accept correction.
Preserve meaningful spiritual experience without making it automatic authority.
avoid: Do not treat intensity, bliss, synchronicity, or a cosmic feeling as proof of external truth or special status.
successSignals: The person can hold the experience while remaining corrigible and grounded.

nodes.title: Keep hypnotic memory vividness separate from historical certainty
recommendations: Treat images, impressions, bodily reactions, and apparent memories as experiences that may be meaningful without assuming they are historically exact.
Use external evidence and ordinary verification for historical claims.
avoid: Do not use hypnosis, ideomotor signals, bodily yes/no responses, or confidence as a truth serum.
successSignals: Experience, interpretation, and historical claim remain separable.

requiredNuance: A vivid or emotionally convincing experience can still be inaccurate in detail or origin.

nodes.title: Stabilize before interpreting an altered state
recommendations: Check medical danger, environment, orientation, body overload, and ability to return before metaphysical interpretation.
Use the smallest intervention that restores present-time choice.
avoid: Do not intensify an unstable altered state in order to learn what it “really” is.
successSignals: The person is oriented enough to examine meaning without being driven by the state.

nodes.title: Use response and boundaries without pretending to settle ontology
recommendations: Start with room, body, basic safety, and the effect of different responses.
Compassion, distance, boundaries, or stopping can be practical choices without deciding what the experience ultimately is.
avoid: Do not use a two-breath response pattern as a diagnostic test of internal part versus external presence.
successSignals: A workable response is found while causal/metaphysical uncertainty remains explicit where unresolved.

nodes.title: For anxiety, start with body and dose before explanation
recommendations: Orient, track activation, locate neutral or supportive contact, and adjust dose before asking for a story.
Use inner-child, breathing, tapping, SE-like tracking, Focusing, or body supports only when they fit the person.
avoid: Do not assume anxiety proves a specific hidden cause.
successSignals: Activation becomes more workable or the person identifies that another form of help is needed.

nodes.title: Use indirect language as a responsive tool, not a covert authority trick
recommendations: Use pacing, awareness verbs, presuppositions, gentle cause-effect bridges, embedded invitations, ethical binds, and other patterns to support absorption and choice.
Keep the wording answerable to the live response.
avoid: Do not use confusion, hidden triggers, amnesia, involuntary identity effects, or covert influence as the point of the technique.
successSignals: Language remains hypnotically rich while the person can correct, reject, or redirect it.

nodes.title: Move certain methods to trained, trauma-informed support when needed
recommendations: When the method, current response, or risk exceeds self-guided capacity, use a trauma-informed clinician trained in that method.
Keep educational explanation available even when unsupervised enactment is not appropriate.
avoid: Do not use the clinician-present label to imply that coercion, overreach, or recovered-memory certainty becomes acceptable.
successSignals: Support matches the actual procedure and current risk rather than the diagnostic label alone.

nodes.title: Vet the practitioner by what they actually do, not the method name alone
recommendations: Ask about training, purpose, consent, pacing, memory claims, response to objection, boundaries, and how sessions end.
Distinguish credentials from demonstrated competence and from the conduct of one reported session.
avoid: Do not approve or reject a practitioner solely because they use a named technique such as regression, ego-state work, or Ericksonian hypnosis.
successSignals: The user can describe the actual procedure and evaluate it against consent, pacing, epistemic, and return criteria.

nodes.title: Use the app as teacher, consultant, and optional voice guide without pretending it has a body
recommendations: Text can teach self-hypnosis, script-writing, theory, and practitioner vetting; voice can optionally guide a user-directed hypnotic session.
The app should ask when information from the body is needed and acknowledge that it lacks embodied observation and human intuition.
avoid: Do not position self-hypnosis as merely a temporary inferior substitute for a human hypnotist.
Do not claim the app can detect unreported bodily changes.
successSignals: The user can become increasingly independent, or use the app to prepare for a suitable practitioner, without the app becoming the authority over their experience.

primaryJourneys: Learn self-hypnosis: choose purpose → induction → responsive invitation → full return → daily practice; add the re-entry cue only after entry and return are familiar.
Inner-child / communion work: induction → inner meeting → responsive invitation → contact-dose adjustment and/or wanted care → full return.
Safety-first route: safety/orientation → capacity before content → dissociation response/full return when needed → trained support when the method or response exceeds self-guided capacity.
Influence / epistemic route: de-hypnosis → analysis/intuition balance → memory caution or nonordinary response check when relevant.
Practitioner bridge: trained support → practitioner vetting, with the app as teacher/consultant rather than a claim of embodied therapist intuition.
